l: battle at Cumorah, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_a battle [great and tremendous] After the great and tremendous battle at Cumorah, the surviving Nephites were hunted and destroyed.

l: disciples of Jesus, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The disciples of Jesus, the remaining people who knew the true God, ministered to Mormon and Moroni before the Lord would not let them remain with the people.

l: land, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The land became a place of continual murder and bloodshed, with only Lamanites and robbers remaining upon it.

l: murder and bloodshed, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The whole face of the land was characterized by continual murder and bloodshed.

l: saints, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Saints who once possessed the land pray for their brethren; from the dust they cry, and the Lord knows their prayers for the record’s coming forth.

l: miracles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Miracles are works performed by God, Jesus Christ, and the apostles through divine power. The record will come forth when people deny them, though faithful people are described moving mountains, shaking earth, overcoming prisons, and receiving protection. God remains a God of miracles; they cease among people through unbelief and departure from the right way.

l: secret combinations, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: cause blood of saints [to cry unto the Lord] Secret combinations and the works of darkness will cause the blood of saints to cry unto the Lord.

l: works of darkness, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: cause blood of saints [to cry unto the Lord] The works of darkness, together with secret combinations, will bring about the cries of the blood of saints.

l: power of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_denied denied [in a future day] The record will come forth by the power of God. This power also enabled faithful people to perform mighty acts and withstand dangers.

l: churches, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: are_polluted polluted [because of pride] Churches become polluted through pride, love of money, fine apparel, and iniquity. Leaders and teachers rise in pride, and some churches are built to obtain gain.

l: holy church of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_polluted_by pride [through hypocritical teachers] The holy church of God is polluted by teachers who sell themselves for that which will canker and are ashamed to take upon themselves the name of Christ.

l: holy word of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_polluted_by teachers [through corruption] People transfigure and pollute the holy word of God to bring damnation upon their souls.

l: revelations of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Revelations of God continue, and denying prophecy, gifts, healing, tongues, and interpretation reflects ignorance of Christ’s gospel.

l: word of God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The word of God brings power, and the revelations of God will be fulfilled despite the wickedness of the people.

l: eternal purposes of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The eternal purposes of the Lord will roll on until all his promises are fulfilled.

l: promises of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Lord’s promises will all be fulfilled, and no one can prevent them.

l: blood of saints, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The blood of saints will cry unto the Lord because of secret combinations and works of darkness.

l: pollutions, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Pollutions will cover the earth, including murders, robbing, lying, deceiving, whoredoms, and other abominations.

l: abominations, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Abominations are built up to obtain gain, and people excuse wickedness by claiming that the Lord will uphold it at the last day.

l: churches built for gain, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Churches built for gain seek money by offering forgiveness of sins in exchange for it.

l: money, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_loved loved [more than the poor and needy] People love money and substance more than they love the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted. Money is also used by churches built for gain.

l: pride, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: pollutes churches [through self-exaltation and fine apparel] Pride causes churches, leaders, teachers, and people to become polluted and to engage in envy, strife, malice, persecution, and other iniquities.

l: fine apparel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_loved loved [more than the poor and needy] People love and wear fine apparel and use it in adorning themselves and their churches while neglecting those in need.

l: poor, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: are_neglected_by churches [despite their need] The poor are loved less than money, substance, fine apparel, and church adornment, and are allowed to pass by without notice.

l: needy, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: are_neglected_by churches [despite their need] The needy are neglected while people pursue money, fine apparel, and the adornment of churches.

l: sick, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: are_neglected_by churches [despite their affliction] The sick are allowed to pass by unnoticed while people focus on worldly possessions and appearances.

l: afflicted, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: are_neglected_by churches [despite their affliction] The afflicted are neglected by people who value worldly praise and possessions over their welfare.

l: sword of vengeance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: hangs_over churches [as judgment approaches] The sword of vengeance hangs over the wicked, and the time soon comes when the Lord will avenge the blood of the saints.

l: the Lamb of God (Jesus Christ), The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_holy holiness The Lamb of God is the one before whom people will stand and whose holiness and glory will be revealed. His blood cleanses those who turn to the Lord and cry to the Father in the name of Jesus.

l: unbelievers, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Unbelievers are warned they will face guilt before God and the Lamb, deemed unworthy in guilt, and urged to repent, cry to the Father, and receive cleansing blood.

l: the scriptures, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: teach God is unchangeable The scriptures teach that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever. Those who deny revelations are said either not to have read the scriptures or not to understand them.

l: the apostles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The apostles wrought many mighty miracles.

l: Jesus Christ's disciples, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Jesus Christ’s disciples are commanded to go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature. The command is given to disciples who should tarry and to all his disciples.

l: the children of men, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Miracles cease among the children of men because they dwindle in unbelief, depart from the right way, and do not know the God in whom they should trust.

l: all men, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: All men are redeemed from the endless sleep of temporal death through the resurrection. They will be awakened by the power of God and stand before his bar for judgment.

l: the children of Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The children of Christ are mentioned as people whom the despisers of the works of the Lord will despise. Such despisers are warned that they shall wonder and perish.

l: the saints, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The prayers of all the saints who have dwelt in the land concern the restoration of the brethren to the knowledge of Christ.

l: the brethren, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: are_the_subject_of prayer [for restoration to the knowledge of Christ] The record is written partly concerning the restoration of the brethren to the knowledge of Christ. The writers seek to rid their garments of the blood of brethren who have dwindled in unbelief.

l: the ends of the earth, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The promise of answered prayer through belief in Christ is given to all, even unto the ends of the earth. Christ’s disciples are also commanded to preach the gospel to every creature, and Christ will confirm his words unto the ends of the earth.

l: the great and last day, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: At the great and last day, unbelievers will be brought to stand before the Lamb of God. They are urged to become spotless, pure, fair, and white through cleansing by the blood of the Lamb.

l: the fall of man, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: brings Jesus Christ The fall of man came through Adam. Because of the fall, Jesus Christ came, followed by the redemption of man.

l: the death of Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: brings the resurrection The death of Christ brings to pass the resurrection and a redemption from an endless sleep. This sleep is identified with temporal death.

l: the second coming of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Lord’s coming brings a great day: elements melt, earth rolls together as a scroll, and people stand before the Lamb of God.

l: the sacrament of Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: requires worthiness [when partaken] People are warned not to partake of the sacrament of Christ unworthily. They are instructed to do all things in worthiness and in the name of Jesus Christ.

l: faith, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_required_for prayer [with firmness unshaken] Those who believe in Christ without doubting may ask the Father in the name of Christ and receive what they ask. Faith is also connected with the prayers for the brethren and with the blessing of the house of Israel.

l: the signs of believers, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Signs following believers in Christ’s name include casting out devils, speaking new tongues, surviving dangers, and healing the sick through laying on hands.

l: the gospel commission, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_given_to Jesus Christ's disciples [to preach to every creature] Jesus Christ commands his disciples to go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature. Believers who are baptized shall be saved, while those who do not believe shall be damned.

l: the blood of the Lamb, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: cleanses unbelievers [from uncleanness at the great and last day] The blood of the Lamb cleanses those who turn to the Lord and seek to be spotless, pure, fair, and white at the great and last day.

l: the plates, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: contain the record The writers say that if their plates had been sufficiently large, they would have written in Hebrew.

l: reformed Egyptian, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is the language of the record [a system of characters used by the writers] The record was written in characters called among the writers the reformed Egyptian. Those characters were handed down and altered according to their manner of speech.

l: Hebrew, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_altered_by the writers of the record [according to their manner of speech] The writers say that Hebrew had also been altered by them. If they could have written in Hebrew, the record would have had no imperfection.

l: The Book of Ether
s: The Book of Ether, recorded by Moroni from twenty-four plates, tells the history of the Jaredites from their departure after the confusion of language at the great tower to their final destruction. Jared and his brother lead their families and friends toward a choice land after the Lord preserves their language, guides them through the wilderness, and prepares them to cross the great sea. The brother of Jared’s faith is central: the Lord makes sixteen stones shine, reveals himself as Jesus Christ, and commands him to write and seal revelations for a future faithful people. Moroni also teaches that the sealed record, witnesses, repentance, baptism, faith, hope, charity, and coming unto Christ matter in God’s work. The people reach the promised land after 344 days in barges and establish kingship with Orihah. Their history becomes a repeated cycle of righteous rule, prosperity, rebellion, secret combinations, captivity, prophetic warning, repentance, and war. Kings including Kib, Shule, Omer, Jared, Emer, Heth, Shez, Riplakish, Morianton, Lib, Com, and others rule amid conflicts over power. Prophets warn that wickedness, idolatry, and secret combinations will destroy the people; at intervals, humility and repentance bring preservation, rain, prosperity, industry, and peace. In the final decline, Ether prophesies to Coriantumr’s people, calling them to believe in God and repent. Moroni uses Ether’s ministry to teach that miracles follow faith and that weakness can become strength through humility and faith. The people reject warnings and continue in war, secret societies, famine, pestilence, and violence. Ether records events while hidden in a rock. A curse, continuing conspiracies, and massive battles reduce the nation to ruin. Coriantumr eventually mourns nearly two million dead and seeks peace, but Shiz refuses. Their armies annihilate one another until only Coriantumr and Shiz remain; Coriantumr kills Shiz and collapses, fulfilling Ether’s words as Ether completes his record.

l: The Book of Ether, The Book of Ether
s: is_a book [of the Book of Mormon] The Book of Ether is the record from which Moroni gives an account of the Jaredites. Its account begins at the tower and continues until the Jaredites were destroyed.

l: Jaredites, The Book of Ether
s: are_ancient_inhabitants north country [destroyed inhabitants] The Jaredites came forth from the great tower with Jared, the brother of Jared, their families, and others. The Lord promised to lead them to a choice land and raise up a great nation from their descendants.

l: Moroni, The Book of Ether
s: Moroni is a person, record keeper, and writer who possesses the record of Moroni and writes part of an account from the tower down to the destruction of the Jaredites. Drawing on the twenty and four plates and writing commanded words according to memory, he recounts ancient inhabitants of the north country, sealed things, faith, and the brother of Jared. He withholds detailed oaths and combinations while warning that secret combinations bring destruction and urging the Gentiles to repent. Though he acknowledges weakness in writing, he testifies that he has seen and spoken with Jesus Christ, records teachings on weakness, grace, faith, hope, and charity, prays for the Gentiles, and commends people to seek Jesus. He concludes by finishing the record of the people’s destruction.

l: record of the Jaredites, The Book of Ether
s: The Book of Ether, taken from twenty-four plates, gives Ether’s genealogy and begins the Jaredites’ account at the tower.

l: twenty and four plates, The Book of Ether
s: contain record of the Jaredites The twenty and four plates were found by the people of Limhi. Moroni takes his account of the Jaredites from them.

l: great tower, The Book of Ether
s: is_a landmark [in the account from Adam's time] Jared, his brother, their families, and others came forth from the great tower when the Lord confounded the language of the people.

l: Ether, The Book of Ether
s: Ether is a descendant of Coriantor, a prophet of the Lord, and a record keeper. Guided by the Spirit of the Lord, he prophesies to the people concerning Christ, this land, the New Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the house of Israel, the remnant of Joseph, and Coriantumr. The people reject and expel him. By day he hides in a cavity of a rock, observing their doings, opposing armies, and destructions. After the Lord’s words are fulfilled, he finishes and hides his record so the people of Limhi later find it. He desires the kingdom of God and salvation in it.

l: Coriantor, The Book of Ether
s: Moron’s son lives in captivity, begets Ether amid prophetic warnings of destruction, and dies in captivity.

l: Moron, The Book of Ether
s: Moron, son of Ethem, reigns wickedly, is challenged, regains the kingdom by overthrowing a mighty man, then is overthrown by another and lives the rest of his days in captivity; he begets Coriantor.

l: Ethem, The Book of Ether
s: Ethem, Ahah’s descendant, obtains the kingdom, practices wickedness throughout his days, faces prophetic warnings during his reign, and begets Moron.

l: Ahah, The Book of Ether
s: Ahah, son of Seth, becomes king, reigns throughout his few days, practices iniquity, and causes much bloodshed.

l: Seth, The Book of Ether
s: Seth, son of Shiblon, is brought into captivity and remains there throughout his life.

l: Com, The Book of Ether
s: Com, son and successor of Coriantum, first ruled half the kingdom for forty-two years, then gained the rest after fighting Amgid. Though unable to prevail against robbers, he protected fleeing prophets, received their prophecies, was blessed in his remaining days, lived to old age, and begat Shiblom.

l: Heth, The Book of Ether
s: Heth, son of Hearthom and Com, embraces old secret plans, dethrones and kills Com, reigns and acts against prophets, then lives captive and perishes by famine.

l: Lib, The Book of Ether
s: Lib, son of Kish and brother of Lib, was a just king of great stature who did good in the sight of the Lord. During his reign serpents were destroyed, hunting expanded southward, and the north filled with inhabitants. A great hunter, he fathered sons and daughters including Hearthom, then gained the kingdom after Gilead’s murder and died fighting Coriantumr.

l: Morianton, The Book of Ether
s: Morianton, a descendant of Riplakish, gathers an army of outcasts, fights for power over cities and land, and becomes king. He wins favor by easing burdens, does justice for the people while indulging his own whoredoms, builds many cities, and presides over great prosperity.

l: Riplakish, The Book of Ether
s: Riplakish, son of Shez, reigned unrighteously, taking many wives and concubines, imposing heavy taxes, building cities, a beautiful throne, and prisons, and exploiting prisoners through forced labor and death penalties. He afflicted the people with whoredoms and abominations until, after forty-two years, they rebelled, killed him, and drove out his descendants.

l: Shez (descendant of Heth), The Book of Ether
s: Shez, Heth’s descendant and sole surviving household member, rebuilds a broken people into a righteous kingdom, remembers the Lord’s deliverance, walks in the Lord’s ways, builds many cities, and lives to an exceedingly old age.

l: Emer, The Book of Ether
s: Emer, Omer’s son and successor, is anointed king, judges righteously for sixty-two years, makes his house strong and rich, and anoints his son Coriantum to succeed him.

l: Omer, The Book of Ether
s: Omer, son of Shule, reigned as king and fathered Jared, Esrom, Coriantumr, Emer, and other children. Jared captured him, and Omer spent half his reign in captivity. Warned in a dream, he fled with his family to Ablom, later dwelt with Nimrah, returned to his inheritance, anointed Emer king, and died old.

l: Shule, The Book of Ether
s: Shule, son of Kib, is king of the kingdom of Shule. Mighty in strength and judgment, he makes steel swords, defeats Corihor, restores Kib, and reigns in righteousness. After defeating Noah’s forces and being rescued from captivity, he gives Corihor power, judges those who revile prophets, rules prosperously without wars, has children, and remembers the Lord’s great deed.

l: Kib, The Book of Ether
s: Kib, Orihah’s son and a king, fathers Corihor, is held captive by him, fathers Shule in old age, and regains his kingdom after Shule defeats Corihor.

l: Orihah, The Book of Ether
s: Orihah, Jared’s son and the people’s king, humbly walks before Lord, teaches ancestral great things, judges righteously, and begins a reign in which the people prosper and become exceedingly rich.

l: Jared, The Book of Ether
s: Jared is Omer’s son and brother of the brother of Jared. He first asks his brother to pray that their language not be confounded and to learn where they should go. He travels with his brother, their families, friends, and people through the wilderness, across the great waters, and into the promised land. Jared has four sons, gathers the people before dying, and agrees that they may have a king. Later, Jared rebels against Omer, gains half the kingdom, takes Omer captive, and loses the kingdom after defeat, becoming sorrowful. He is then anointed king through wickedness, gives his daughter to Akish, and is murdered by Akish while on his throne.

l: brother of Jared, The Book of Ether
s: The brother of Jared is a large and mighty man, highly favored of the Lord, with Jared’s families. He begins by crying to the Lord, who preserves the language of Jared, their friends, and families and directs their gathering and journey. After chastening because he had not called upon the Lord, he repents, builds barges with his brethren, and seeks help for breathing, steering, and light. He makes sixteen small stones; the Lord makes them shine, and he places them in the vessels for light. His exceedingly great faith leads him to see the finger of the Lord, Jesus Christ, all things beyond the veil, and great and marvelous things. He writes what he sees on plates in a language that cannot be read, receives two stones, and is commanded to seal them until the Lord shows them to the children of men. A seer with perfect knowledge of God and redemption from the fall, he teaches his people humility, gathers them before death, warns against a king, and by faith commands the mountain Zerin to move.

l: the Lord, The Book of Ether
s: The Lord is a deity and lord of the land who responds with compassion, justice, mercy, guidance, and wrath. At the great tower, he confounds language and scatters the people, yet has compassion on Jared, the brother of Jared, their friends, and their families. He leads them through the wilderness and across the deep toward a choice promised land, gathers flocks and seed, meets and blesses Jared, and raises a great nation from their seed and companions. He appears in a cloud, goes before them, directs their journey, gives instructions for barges, makes stones shine in darkness, protects the vessels from the waters, and brings them safely onward when they cry to him. The Lord requires people on the land to act rightly and remember his works. He does not work in secret combinations, forbids murder and bloodshed, and warns nations supporting such acts to repent or face destruction. He favors and prospers rulers who do good, while those who commit wickedness may be cut off from his presence. Later, he warns Omer in a dream, removes a curse from the land, sends blessings, rain, and preservation from famine when people humble themselves and repent, and has mercy in proportion to repentance. He sends prophets and his word to call the people back. When they reject his voice and ripen in iniquity, his Spirit no longer strives with them; he visits them in wrath. He offers Coriantumr and his household the kingdom if they repent, but his prophecies are fulfilled in the people’s destruction, after which he speaks again to Ether.

l: language of the people, The Book of Ether
s: is_confounded scattering of the people [at the great tower, except for Jared, his brother, and their associates] The language of the people was confounded by the Lord at the great tower, causing the people to be scattered. The language of Jared, the brother of Jared, and their friends was not confounded.

l: valley of Nimrod, The Book of Ether
s: A northward valley named after Nimrod, where the Lord directed the brother of Jared and gathered people to go down and meet Him.

l: north country, The Book of Ether
s: The ancient inhabitants described by Moroni were destroyed by the hand of the Lord upon the face of the north country.

l: confounding of the language, The Book of Ether
s: The confounding of the language occurred at the great tower when the Lord swore that the people should be scattered over the face of the earth. Jared’s people and their friends were spared from this confounding.

l: scattering of the people, The Book of Ether
s: occurs earth [upon all the face of the earth] The people were scattered upon all the face of the earth according to the word of the Lord after their language was confounded.

l: journey to the promised land, The Book of Ether
s: begins_at valley which is northward [after gathering the people and possessions] The Lord told the brother of Jared to gather the people and go into the valley which is northward, promising to go before them into a choice land.

l: land of promise, The Book of Ether
s: Land of promise is a land choice above all other lands, preserved by God for a righteous people and possessed under the Lord. Its possessors must serve the true and only God; if they do, their nation is free from bondage and captivity, but if they do not, they may be swept off in the fulness of God’s wrath. It contains fruit, grain, silks, fine linen, gold, silver, precious things, useful animals, and many cities, and it contains New Jerusalem. Jared, the brother of Jared, with families and friends, is promised leadership into it. It is restored to Omer and prospers under Emer, then repeatedly is rebuilt and populated after destruction and war, becoming rich and industrious. Yet wickedness brings dearth, famine, serpents, wars, pestilence, calamity, destruction, and warnings to repent. Finally, a great curse covers all the land with the dead; New Jerusalem is to be built upon it for the remnant of the seed of Joseph.

l: great nation, The Book of Ether
s: is_greatest nation [upon all the face of the earth] The Lord promised to raise up a great nation from the seed of Jared, the brother of Jared, and those who would go with them. He said none would be greater than that nation upon all the face of the earth.

l: wilderness, The Book of Ether
s: contains barges [used to cross many waters] The wilderness is the region through which Jared, the brother of Jared, and their companions travel after the Lord commands them to go where no man had been. They build barges in the wilderness and cross many waters while being continually directed by the Lord.

l: God, The Book of Ether
s: God is the true and only deity the land’s inhabitants must serve, manifested by Jesus Christ. He brings wrath on nations ripened in iniquity, grants wisdom, witnesses, manifestations, and miracles according to faith, and receives the repentant into his kingdom. He gives the law of Moses, prepares a more excellent way through the gift of his Son, and shows Himself after faith.

l: Gentiles, The Book of Ether
s: The Gentiles are called and commanded to repent of iniquity and sins, become clean, exercise faith in Jesus Christ, and come unto Him. Greater hidden knowledge is promised through faith and sanctification. They are warned not to let murderous or secret combinations gain power, but to awake when they appear. Though they may mock Moroni’s weak writing, they are urged toward meekness, humility, faith, hope, charity, grace, and a prepared place.

l: Moriancumer, The Book of Ether
s: Moriancumer is a seashore place where Jared and his brethren pitch tents and dwell for four years.

l: great deep, The Book of Ether
s: The great sea divides the lands, and Jared and his brethren reach it after traveling through the wilderness. They pitch their tents beside it at Moriancumer and are later prepared to cross its great depth in barges.

l: vessels or barges, The Book of Ether
s: The vessels or barges are small, light upon the water, and exceedingly tight like a dish and the ark of Noah. With peaked ends, a tight-shut door, no light, and air holes in the top and bottom, they carry people, food, flocks, herds, beasts, animals, and fowls safely across the great water and sea.

l: people, The Book of Ether
s: A group that begins with Jared, his brother, and about twenty-two souls is taught humility, crosses the great waters, praises the Lord, and settles the promised land. They multiply, grow strong, cultivate the earth, and seek a king. Under rulers such as Orihah and Shule they prosper and become exceedingly numerous, though rebellions lead them into wickedness, idolatries, and mockery of prophets. Repeated repentance brings renewed prosperity. Secret combinations under Akish corrupt them and lead to devastating war, nearly destroying them. Rebuilt under Shez, they spread across the land, endure rebellion and war, and prosper under Morianton through trade, mining, crafts, agriculture, animal husbandry, and weapons-making. In later periods they reject, persecute, and kill prophets, harden their hearts, and suffer wars, famine, pestilence, destruction, captivity, dearth, and poisonous serpents; some eventually repent and cry unto the Lord.

l: Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Ether
s: Spirit persuades people to do good and know truth, yet does not always strive with man and ceases before final battles.

l: wickedness, The Book of Ether
s: Wickedness, including idolatry, secret plans, robbery, and all manner of wrongdoing, fills the land, brings a curse, and will lead to destruction unless the people repent.

l: decrees of God, The Book of Ether
s: concern land of promise [the land is a land of promise] The decrees of God concerning the land state that it is a land of promise and that any nation possessing it must serve God or be swept off when ripened in iniquity. The decrees are presented so the Gentiles may repent and avoid bringing down the fulness of God’s wrath.

l: the fullness of the Lord's wrath, The Book of Ether
s: comes_upon inhabitants of the land [when they are ripened in iniquity] The fulness of the wrath of God comes upon the inhabitants of the land when they are ripened in iniquity. Nations that possess the land and do not serve God are threatened with being swept off.

l: building of the barges, The Book of Ether
s: is_done_by brother of Jared [with his brethren] The building of the barges begins after the Lord commands the brother of Jared to work according to the manner of the barges previously built. The brother of Jared and his brethren build them according to the Lord’s instructions, making them small, light, and tight.

l: light, The Book of Ether
s: Light is absent from the barges before preparation by the Lord, prompting the brother of Jared’s concern about crossing the great water in darkness. The Lord rejects windows and fire; stones then provide continual light in the vessels, above or under water.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the God of the land, the Father and the Son, and the Son of God. Prepared from the foundation of the world, he redeems mankind through belief in his name so that all may have life. He shows himself in flesh and blood to people of faith, including the brother of Jared, reveals knowledge through great works, and has power to show all things. He gives the brother of Jared two stones and commands him to write, seal, and hide what he saw; these things are withheld from the Gentiles until they repent and become clean. He is truthful and unable to lie. The record teaches that those who repent and come unto the Father in Jesus’s name will be received into the kingdom of God, and that a nation on the choice land may be free if it serves him. He loves the children of men, lays down his life for the world, takes it again, and prepares a place and a way for others to partake of the heavenly gift.

l: sea, The Book of Ether
s: The sea has furious winds, mountain waves, deep waters, and terrible tempests that bury the vessels or barges. No monster of the sea or whale breaks or mars them, and the people travel upon the sea for 344 days.

l: small stones, The Book of Ether
s: Sixteen small, white and clear stones are made from a rock for light in vessels or barges. The finger of the Lord touches them one by one so they shine. The brother of Jared places one in each end, where they give continual light in darkness above or under the water.

l: two stones, The Book of Ether
s: Two stones given by Jesus Christ to the brother of Jared are sealed with his writings and will magnify them in the Lord’s due time.

l: finger of the Lord, The Book of Ether
s: The finger of the Lord, like flesh and blood, touches stones; the brother of Jared sees it and falls with fear.

l: mankind, The Book of Ether
s: Mankind is created after the image of God and may receive eternal life through Jesus Christ by believing on his name; all earth’s inhabitants are shown across time.

l: children of men, The Book of Ether
s: Children of men receive weakness to become humble; with faith, weak things become strong, and hope and charity lead to inheritance in the prepared place.

l: fall, The Book of Ether
s: The fall makes human natures evil continually, but redemption through Jesus Christ overcomes it through faith.

l: incarnation, The Book of Ether
s: is_foretold_by Jesus Christ [as taking upon himself flesh and blood] Jesus Christ says that he will take upon himself flesh and blood. He says that he will appear to his people in the flesh as he appears to the brother of Jared in the spirit.

l: redemption, The Book of Ether
s: Jesus Christ overcomes the fall, redeeming the brother of Jared and bringing him back into his presence.

l: faith, The Book of Ether
s: Faith enables knowledge of Jesus Christ and revelation, including the brother of Jared seeing the finger of the Lord through exceeding faith. Exercised in Jesus Christ, it leads to sanctification, salvation, spiritual manifestations, and the revelations received by the brother of Jared. It is hope for unseen things and produces hope for a better world, good works, steadfast souls, miracles, promises, and strength after trials. It culminates in witnesses and divine manifestations, including a promise to three disciples.

l: knowledge, The Book of Ether
s: The Lord brings redemption from the fall, speaks truth, and shows all things; the brother of Jared’s knowledge lets him behold within the veil.

l: flesh and blood, The Book of Ether
s: Jesus Christ, initially unknown by the brother of Jared as having flesh and blood, teaches that he will assume flesh and blood and appear in the flesh.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Ether
s: Jesus Christ is the Son of God and Father of the heavens, earth, and all things in them. As the world’s light, life, and truth, he leads all good and commands people to repent, come unto him, believe his gospel, and be baptized. After being lifted up upon the cross, he shows himself to humanity and directs that the brother of Jared’s visions be revealed after he has shown himself to his people. He sanctifies faithful Gentiles and manifests greater, marvelous things to them, while condemning those who deny or contend against his word.

l: the Father, The Book of Ether
s: The Father is God, who sent Jesus Christ, remembers his covenant with the fathers of the house of Israel, and has begun his work across the land. He bears record of the word and work of God. Those who repent and come to him in Jesus’ name will be received into the kingdom of God. Christ glorified his name, and his mansions hold a prepared place for mankind.

l: the house of Israel, The Book of Ether
s: The house of Israel possesses Jerusalem, includes the remnant of the seed of Joseph, and is tied to the covenant with Abraham. Great things laid up by the Father will be revealed as it rends unbelief, calls with a broken heart and contrite spirit, and learns that the Father remembers the covenant with its fathers.

l: people, The Book of Ether
s: The people reject Ether’s words, remain unrepentant, and experience widespread wickedness. Under Satan’s power, their hearts are hard and minds blind. Because of the curse upon the land, they cling to property, refuse borrowing or lending, and carry swords for defense. They divide between the armies of Shiz and Coriantumr as war, secret violence, robbery, bloodshed, deaths, displacement, and destruction spread. After many days of fighting, only a few remain.

l: plates, The Book of Ether
s: The plates contain great and marvelous things, including what the brother of Jared saw. Their writings and interpretation are sealed by commandment of the Lord. They may be shown to those assisting in bringing forth the work, but not touched for translation unless wisdom in God permits.

l: record, The Book of Ether
s: indicates work of the Father [when received] The record is to be received as a sign that the work of the Father has commenced upon all the face of the land.

l: gospel of Christ, The Book of Ether
s: People throughout the earth are commanded to believe in the gospel of Christ. Those who believe and are baptized in Jesus Christ’s name shall be saved.

l: revelations, The Book of Ether
s: are_unfolded house of Israel [when the veil of unbelief is rent] The Lord promises to manifest all his revelations to those who exercise faith as the brother of Jared did. The revelations caused to be written by his servant John will be unfolded in the eyes of all the people when the time is at hand.

l: manifestations of the Spirit, The Book of Ether
s: are_given_to believers [who believe the words of Jesus Christ] Jesus Christ will visit those who believe his words with the manifestations of his Spirit, and they shall know and bear record.

l: unbelief, The Book of Ether
s: causes great and marvelous things [to remain hidden] Unbelief causes knowledge and great things to remain hidden and leads people to remain in wickedness, hardness of heart, and blindness of mind. The veil of unbelief must be rent before the great and marvelous things can be made manifest.

l: repentance, The Book of Ether
s: Repentance is required for Coriantumr and his household to preserve the kingdom and spare the people. Gentiles and all the ends of the earth are commanded to repent, become clean, and come unto Jesus Christ. Corihor and later the people repent and prosper; prophets call repeatedly, and the Lord shows mercy when people repent. Coriantumr, his household, and the people do not repent.

l: baptism, The Book of Ether
s: leads_to salvation [when accompanied by belief] People are commanded to be baptized in Jesus Christ’s name. He that believes and is baptized shall be saved, while he that believes not shall be damned.

l: work of the Father, The Book of Ether
s: commences land [upon all the face of the land when the record is received] The work of the Father has commenced upon all the face of the land when the record is received.

l: great and marvelous things, The Book of Ether
s: The great and marvelous things hidden from the house of Israel from the foundation of the world will be made manifest when they rend the veil of unbelief and call upon the Father with a broken heart and contrite spirit.

l: three witnesses, The Book of Ether
s: Three witnesses are shown plates by God’s power and know with certainty that these things are true.

l: work, The Book of Ether
s: A work established by three witnesses, showing forth God’s power and word, stands as testimony against the world at the last day.

l: the Son, The Book of Ether
s: bears_record_of word of God The Son is named as one who bears record of the work.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Book of Ether
s: The Holy Ghost bears record of God the Father, the Lord Jesus Christ, and the work; it enables much speaking, and Moroni asks that it abide in people forever.

l: testimony, The Book of Ether
s: stands_against the world [at the last day] The testimony of three witnesses, together with the work and the records of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, will stand as a testimony against the world at the last day.

l: Noah, The Book of Ether
s: Noah, son of Corihor, rebels against Shule and Corihor, becomes king over part of the land, captures Shule in Moron, and is killed by Shule’s sons while preparing to kill Shule.

l: promised land, The Book of Ether
s: is_tilled_by people (Jared and his brother's people) The promised land is the destination toward which the wind drives the people. After landing there, they till the earth, multiply, and become strong.

l: wind, The Book of Ether
s: blows_towards promised land [during the voyage across the great waters] The Lord causes a furious wind to blow toward the promised land. The wind never ceases while the people are upon the waters and drives them forward.

l: bringing them across the great deep, The Book of Ether
s: A voyage upon the water lasts 344 days as people cross great waters in vessels, endure tempests, are driven by wind, and praise the Lord.

l: landing in the promised land, The Book of Ether
s: occurs_in promised land [on its shore] The people land upon the shore of the promised land after 344 days upon the water. They bow down, humble themselves before the Lord, and shed tears of joy because of his tender mercies.

l: anointing a king, The Book of Ether
s: is_desired_by people (Jared and his brother's people) [to establish a king over them] The people request that one of the sons of Jared or the brother of Jared be anointed king. After several sons refuse, Orihah is anointed king over the people.

l: kingship, The Book of Ether
s: leads_to captivity [according to the brother of Jared] The brother of Jared says that kingship will lead into captivity, while Jared allows the people to choose a king. The chosen sons refuse except Orihah, who begins to reign and leads the people into prosperity.

l: captivity, The Book of Ether
s: Captivity is a recurring condition prophesied by the brother of Jared when a king is taken captive. Kib, Kim, several descendants, Seth, Moron, and Coriantor remain captive for life or into old age. Shule is captured but freed by his sons; Levi serves forty-two years before gaining the kingdom.

l: prosperity, The Book of Ether
s: The people became exceedingly rich under Morianton in buildings, gold, silver, grain, flocks, and herds. Under Lib and the following period, they were described as exceedingly blessed and prospered by the hand of the Lord.

l: Corihor, The Book of Ether
s: Corihor, son of Kib, rebels, settles in Nehor, draws followers, and captures Moron’s king. Shule defeats him and restores Kib. Corihor later repents, receives power in Shule’s kingdom, and has exceedingly fair sons and daughters, including Noah.

l: the prophets, The Book of Ether
s: Prophets are sent by Lord among the people during Shule’s reign to warn that wickedness and idolatry bring a curse and destruction unless they repent; though reviled and mocked, Shule lets them travel throughout the land.

l: kingdom of Shule, The Book of Ether
s: is_ruled_by Shule The kingdom of Shule is established when Shule receives the kingdom from Kib. It remains under Shule’s rule after the land is divided, and Nimrod gives the kingdom of Cohor to Shule.

l: judgment, The Book of Ether
s: is_executed in righteousness [by Orihah and Shule] Orihah executes judgment in righteousness throughout his days, and Shule is mighty in judgment. Shule executes judgment against those who revile the prophets and continues to execute judgment in righteousness throughout his reign.

l: rebellion, The Book of Ether
s: is_committed_by Corihor [against his father] Corihor rebels against his father Kib and draws away many people. Noah later rebels against Shule and Corihor, drawing away Cohor, his brethren, and many of the people.

l: battle, The Book of Ether
s: Battle is fought between Shule and Corihor: Shule gains the kingdom, later defeats and slays Cohor, while later wars recur over control of the land and kingdom.

l: idolatry, The Book of Ether
s: brings curse upon the land [together with wickedness] The prophets warn that the people’s idolatry is bringing a curse upon the land. When the people repent of their idolatries, the Lord spares them and they prosper again.

l: the curse upon the land, The Book of Ether
s: The curse upon the land comes as a consequence of wickedness and destroys the people when they are ripened in iniquity. It makes tools and swords disappear by the following day, causing people to hold tightly to property and avoid borrowing or lending. The Lord begins taking it away during Emer’s reign, but prophets warn it will return without repentance.

l: wars, The Book of Ether
s: are_absent no more [in the days of Shule] The people engage in wars during the conflicts involving Corihor, Noah, and Cohor. There are no more wars in the days of Shule.

l: Coriantumr, The Book of Ether
s: Coriantumr is Omer’s child and a king over all the land who possesses the kingdom through his sons. Skilled in every art of war, he initially refuses repentance despite prophecy. Captured and wounded in the thigh by Shared, he is freed by his sons, kills Shared, and cannot fight for two years. He later defeats Gilead and Lib, kills Lib at Agosh, and flees Shiz before suffering many deep wounds near the seashore and hill Comnor. After recovering, he remembers Ether’s words, mourns the destruction of nearly two million people, repents, and offers Shiz the kingdom to spare the people. He continues leading battles, kills Shiz, and falls as if lifeless.

l: Akish, The Book of Ether
s: Akish, son of Kimnor and friend of Omer, seeks Jared’s daughter and power. After Jared promises her for Omer’s head, he leads kindred and friends through oaths and fair promises in a secret combination, overthrows Omer, marries Jared’s daughter, murders Jared, becomes king, kills one son by starvation, and wars with his other sons.

l: Satan, The Book of Ether
s: Satan is a liar and builder of secret combinations who seeks power over people’s hearts, causing murder and opposition to prophets until people are persuaded to do good continually.

l: daughter of Jared, The Book of Ether
s: Jared's daughter, exceedingly expert and fair, devises a kingdom-redemption plan, teaches Jared secret plans, and dances before Akish to secure marriage.

l: kingdom, The Book of Ether
s: The kingdom is sought by Jared for worldly glory. Jared gains half through flattery but loses it after defeat, prompting his daughter’s plan to restore him. It later alternates between righteous building, rebellion, war, captivity, succession, division, and repeated struggles for power under rulers from Shez through Moron.

l: captivity of Omer, The Book of Ether
s: is_a captivity [lasting half of Omer's days] Omer was carried into captivity by Jared and served in captivity for half of his reign. During that time, he begat Esrom and Coriantumr.

l: Jared's rebellion, The Book of Ether
s: is_against Omer [Jared's father] Jared rebelled against Omer, moved to the land of Heth, and used cunning words to gain half the kingdom. He then gave battle to Omer and made him serve in captivity.

l: battles against Jared, The Book of Ether
s: Battles occurred between Coriantumr and the brother of Shared, Gilead, Lib, and Shiz. The battle at hill Comnor became exceedingly sore, and Shiz gave Coriantumr many deep wounds.

l: daughter of Jared's dance, The Book of Ether
s: pleases Akish [so that he desired her as a wife] Jared's daughter danced before Akish and pleased him so that he desired her as a wife. Jared offered her to Akish if Akish would bring Omer's head.

l: oaths of the ancients, The Book of Ether
s: Ancient oaths, handed down from Cain through seekers of power, are administered by Akish to bind kindred and friends to secrecy and assistance.

l: the secret combinations of Akish and his friends, The Book of Ether
s: Akish and his friends form a wicked, secret combination through oaths and fair promises. Seeking power, gain, and the kingdom, it overthrows Omer, spreads corruption through the people, and causes rebellion and rejection of prophets. It ultimately fights against Coriantumr, with many slain, illustrating the destructive threat such combinations pose to freedom in all lands, nations, and countries.

l: power, The Book of Ether
s: is_sought_by secret combination [for gain] The secret combination was formed to obtain power and was kept up by the power of the devil. Moroni warned that combinations seeking power would overthrow freedom and bring destruction.

l: power and gain, The Book of Ether
s: is_sought_by secret combination [through power] The combinations were built to obtain gain as well as power. Nations that uphold them until they spread over the nation are warned that they will be destroyed.

l: murder, The Book of Ether
s: is_forbidden_by God [from the beginning of man] The oaths supported murder, plunder, lying, and other wickedness. The Lord forbids the shedding of blood, and the blood of those slain is described as crying from the ground for vengeance.

l: freedom, The Book of Ether
s: is_threatened_by secret combination [in all lands, nations, and countries] Secret combinations seek to overthrow the freedom of all lands, nations, and countries. Their spread brings the destruction of all people.

l: Coriantum, The Book of Ether
s: Coriantum succeeds Emer, reigns forty-nine years, builds mighty cities and administers good, yet dwells in captivity; old age brings a young wife and children including Com.

l: the house of Omer, The Book of Ether
s: The house of Omer, Emer’s ruling house, includes Omer’s family and fugitives, survives near-total destruction, and later dwells with Omer after Nimrah flees.

l: the sons of Akish, The Book of Ether
s: The sons of Akish seek gain, offer money to draw people, win most hearts through sworn iniquity, and enter war with Akish.

l: the land southward, The Book of Ether
s: Zarahemla, the land southward, was preserved as wilderness for hunting food after poisonous serpents were destroyed.

l: the overthrow of Omer's kingdom, The Book of Ether
s: is_caused_by the secret combinations of Akish and his friends The overthrow of Omer’s kingdom is caused by the secret combinations of Akish and his friends. Omer escapes after receiving a warning from the Lord, while Jared is made king.

l: the murder of Jared, The Book of Ether
s: Akish uses the oath of the ancients through a secret society to have Jared murdered on his throne while he gives audience.

l: the war between the sons of Akish and Akish, The Book of Ether
s: lasts many years The war between the sons of Akish and Akish lasts many years. It results in the destruction of nearly all the people of the kingdom, except for thirty souls and those who flee with the house of Omer.

l: the destruction of nearly all the people, The Book of Ether
s: is_caused_by the war between the sons of Akish and Akish The destruction of nearly all the people occurs during the long war between the sons of Akish and Akish. Only thirty souls and those who flee with the house of Omer are spared.

l: the reign of Coriantum, The Book of Ether
s: Riplakish reigned for forty-two years, Morianton reigned after establishing himself as king, Kim reigned eight years, and Com reigned over half the kingdom for forty-two years. Hearthom reigned twenty-four years before the kingdom was taken from him.

l: the great famine, The Book of Ether
s: The great famine, caused by absent rain and failure to repent, brings dearth that rapidly destroys inhabitants until repentance leads the Lord to send rain.

l: the poisonous serpents, The Book of Ether
s: Poisonous serpents come upon the land, poison many people, and hedge up the way so people attempting to pass may fall by them. In the days of Lib, they are destroyed; afterward, the people enter the land southward to hunt food.

l: the repentance of the people, The Book of Ether
s: The repentance of the people begins amid famine as they cry unto the Lord, then culminates in sufficient humility, rain, and preservation from famine.

l: the rain, The Book of Ether
s: revives the people The rain is sent by the Lord after the people humble themselves before him. It causes the people to revive and fruit to appear in the north countries and the surrounding countries.

l: robbers, The Book of Ether
s: Robbers killed Shez’s eldest son for riches, then arose again in Com’s days, used ancient oaths and plans, and sought to destroy the kingdom.

l: the land northward, The Book of Ether
s: is_covered_with the people [the whole face of the land] The whole face of the land northward was covered with inhabitants. It was part of a choice land in which the people prospered and conducted extensive industry and commerce.

l: cities, The Book of Ether
s: Shez built many cities, and the people spread over the land. Morianton also built many cities, and Com gained power over many cities during his wars.

l: rebellion against Riplakish, The Book of Ether
s: causes war [again in the land] After Riplakish had reigned for forty-two years, the people rose up in rebellion against him. War followed, Riplakish was killed, and his descendants were driven out of the land.

l: taxation, The Book of Ether
s: Riplakish imposed heavy taxes on the people and used the taxes to build many spacious buildings. Those who would not pay or could not pay were cast into prison, and prisoners were forced to labor.

l: commerce, The Book of Ether
s: exists_between the people [through buying, selling, and trafficking] The people were exceedingly industrious and bought, sold, and trafficked with one another to gain wealth.

l: mining and metallurgy, The Book of Ether
s: includes gold [and silver, iron, brass, copper, and other metals] The people worked in every manner of ore and made gold, silver, iron, brass, copper, and other metals. They dug ores from the earth, cast up mighty heaps of earth, refined materials, and produced fine workmanship, tools, weapons, cloth, and other goods.

l: prophets, The Book of Ether
s: Prophets warn the people to repent, forsake wickedness, and turn to the Lord or face destruction and judgment. Rejected and pursued, they seek protection, are killed or withdraw, yet continue foretelling another people possessing the land.

l: the destruction of the people, The Book of Ether
s: The destruction of the people, prophesied by Ether, unfolds in all the land after warnings to repent. Moroni records it and Ether observes from a rock as wars, famines, pestilences, and wickedness bring unparalleled destruction, including Coriantumr’s household.

l: wickedness, The Book of Ether
s: The people were warned to forsake their wickedness and repent of their iniquities. Wickedness continued among their rulers and people and led to bloodshed and destruction.

l: Shiblom, The Book of Ether
s: Shiblom reigns over the people after Com, then is slain amid great destruction and calamity.

l: brother of Shiblom, The Book of Ether
s: Brother of Shiblom rebels against him and causes prophets warning of destruction to be put to death.

l: war, The Book of Ether
s: War is an exceedingly great, lasting conflict throughout all the land. It begins after the brother of Shiblom rebels, continues without ceasing as Coriantumr, his household, and the people do not repent, and culminates in the armies of Shiz and Coriantumr leaving the land covered with unburied dead.

l: calamity, The Book of Ether
s: Great calamity came upon all the land because the people rejected warnings of a curse and destruction.

l: wicked combinations, The Book of Ether
s: prevent_hearkening_to Lord The people did not hearken to the voice of the Lord because of their wicked combinations. These combinations contributed to wars, contentions, and destruction.

l: famines, The Book of Ether
s: occur_in the land [many] Many famines occurred throughout the land as part of the great destruction that had never been known upon the face of the earth.

l: pestilences, The Book of Ether
s: occur_in the land [many] Many pestilences occurred throughout the land along with wars and famines, contributing to the great destruction.

l: bloodshed and carnage, The Book of Ether
s: Bloodshed and carnage lasts long and spreads across the land, leaving men, women, and children dead and unburied as war moves swiftly between battles.

l: rebellion, The Book of Ether
s: arises_from secret combination [built up to get power and gain] A rebellion arose among the people because of the secret combination built up to obtain power and gain. A mighty man used the rebellion to overthrow half of Moron's kingdom.

l: mighty man (Moron's challenger), The Book of Ether
s: A mighty man arises in iniquity, battles Moron, overthrows and maintains half the kingdom for years before Moron overthrows him.

l: overthrow, The Book of Ether
s: Moron overthrew the mighty man who had taken half of the kingdom and obtained the kingdom again. Another mighty man then overthrew Moron and obtained the kingdom.

l: mighty man (Moron's successor), The Book of Ether
s: A descendant of the brother of Jared arises, overthrows Moron, and obtains the kingdom.

l: judgment, The Book of Ether
s: is_executed_by Lord [against the people for failure to repent] Prophets warned that the Lord God would execute judgment against the people to their utter destruction unless they repented of their iniquities.

l: another people, The Book of Ether
s: possesses the land [by the Lord's power] Prophets warned that the Lord God would send or bring forth another people to possess the land after the manner by which he brought the people's fathers.

l: gift of his Son, The Book of Ether
s: is_a more excellent way [prepared by God] The gift of His Son provides a more excellent way through which the law is fulfilled and people may partake of the heavenly gift. Partaking of this gift is connected with faith.

l: hope, The Book of Ether
s: is_needed_for inheritance [in the place prepared for man] Hope comes from faith and provides an anchor to the souls of men, making them sure and steadfast in good works. People must hope to receive an inheritance in the place prepared for them.

l: charity, The Book of Ether
s: Charity is Christ’s love for the children of men, required for people to inherit their prepared place in the Father’s mansions.

l: miracles, The Book of Ether
s: are_wrought_by faith [among those before and after Christ] Miracles are wrought by faith, including the prison’s collapse, the conversion of the Lamanites, and the moving of the mountain Zerin. No one has wrought miracles until after having faith.

l: mansions of my Father, The Book of Ether
s: is_a place prepared for man [among the mansions of the Father] The mansions of the Father contain a prepared place where man may have a more excellent hope. Inheritance in that place requires hope and charity.

l: grace of God, The Book of Ether
s: The grace of God may abide forever, is sufficient for humble people, and makes weak things strong through humility and faith.

l: weakness, The Book of Ether
s: is_given_to children of men [so they may be humble] Moroni acknowledges weakness in writing and fears that the Gentiles will mock his words. The Lord says weakness is given so people may be humble and promises to make weak things strong when they humble themselves and have faith.

l: the remnant of the seed of Joseph, The Book of Ether
s: A remnant of the house of Joseph inherits this land, is numbered among Israel, and builds the holy New Jerusalem, dwelling there with garments made white through the blood of the Lamb.

l: New Jerusalem, The Book of Ether
s: New Jerusalem is a holy city and sanctuary that comes down from heaven, is built upon this land for Joseph’s remnant, and blesses those who dwell there.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Ether
s: Jerusalem is a holy city for the house of Israel, to be destroyed and built up again; its inhabitants are scattered, gathered, and partake of Abraham’s covenant.

l: the cavity of a rock, The Book of Ether
s: The cavity of a rock is where Ether hides by day after being cast out and where he makes the remainder of his record while viewing the destructions by night.

l: the record of Moroni, The Book of Ether
s: The record of Moroni concerns the destruction of the people, and Moroni proceeds to finish it in this unit.

l: the prophecies of Ether, The Book of Ether
s: The prophecies of Ether are described as great and marvelous and concern Christ, the New Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the house of Israel, and the destruction of the people.

l: the words of Ether, The Book of Ether
s: Ether prophesies New Jerusalem and the land’s destiny, but the people reject all his words and warnings.

l: the New Jerusalem prophecy, The Book of Ether
s: The New Jerusalem prophecy states that a New Jerusalem will be built upon this land for the remnant of the seed of Joseph and that it will be a holy city of the Lord.

l: the covenant God made with Abraham, The Book of Ether
s: is_fulfilled_for the house of Israel [through gathering] The covenant God made with Abraham is fulfilled for those who were scattered and gathered from the four quarters of the earth and from the north countries.

l: the blood of the Lamb, The Book of Ether
s: washes garments [making them white] The blood of the Lamb makes the garments of those in the New Jerusalem white and washes the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

l: Ether's expulsion, The Book of Ether
s: precedes the great war [in the same year] Ether is cast out from among the people after they reject his prophecies. He hides in the cavity of a rock and continues making his record.

l: the great war, The Book of Ether
s: is_a war [among the people] The great war begins in the year Ether is cast out, as mighty men rise against Coriantumr with secret plans of wickedness.

l: Shiz, The Book of Ether
s: Shiz, proposed ruler and leader of armies and people, refused to spare Coriantumr’s people unless Coriantumr surrendered. He led repeated battles and pursued Coriantumr, then fainted from blood loss and was killed by him.

l: secret combinations, The Book of Ether
s: Secret combinations strengthened Gilead’s army, then murdered him in a secret pass and gave the kingdom to Lib.

l: army of Coriantumr, The Book of Ether
s: Army of Coriantumr gains great strength in the wilderness, gathers on hill Comnor, pursues Shared’s brother, battles Lib and Shiz, and ultimately makes Shiz’s people flee.

l: people of Shiz, The Book of Ether
s: The people of Shiz, feared throughout the land, pursued Coriantumr in war, overthrowing cities and killing women and children. Armed men, women, and children fought at the seashore and hill Comnor, suffering great destruction. Angered again, they gathered for four years and fought Coriantumr’s people until nearly all fell by the sword.

l: destruction, The Book of Ether
s: Destruction, prepared by wickedness and abominations, unfolds among Shiz’s army in battle with Coriantumr, terrifying people as cities burn and women and children are slain.

l: people of Coriantumr, The Book of Ether
s: People aligned with Coriantumr, angered at people of Shiz, gather armed men, women, and children for four years and fight until nearly all fall by the sword.

l: battle, The Book of Ether
s: is_fought_at waters of Ripliancum [after the armies gathered there] The battle between the people of Coriantumr and the people of Shiz continued for years of gathering and then through repeated days of fighting. The armies suffered immense losses, and the final battle ended with Coriantumr killing Shiz.

l: death, The Book of Ether
s: Death came to nearly two million people, including mighty men, their wives, and their children. Continued battles left only Coriantumr and Shiz, and Shiz died after Coriantumr smote off his head.

l: The Book of Moroni
s: This document is Moroni’s continuing record after completing an abridgment of the people of Jared. Hiding from the Lamanites and refusing to deny Christ amid warfare and killings, Moroni preserves teachings intended to benefit future readers, including the Lamanites. He records Christ’s instructions to twelve disciples to pray and confer the Holy Ghost by laying on hands, then describes ordaining priests and teachers to preach repentance and remission of sins through Jesus Christ. He gives church practices for administering bread and wine in remembrance of Christ’s body and blood, and for baptism, membership, repentance, forgiveness, fasting, prayer, and meetings led by the Holy Ghost. Mormon’s teachings follow: people should distinguish good from evil, exercise faith in Jesus Christ, hope through his atonement and resurrection, and seek charity, the pure love of Christ. In an epistle to Moroni, Mormon teaches that little children are alive in Christ and need neither repentance nor baptism; he condemns their baptism and warns of Nephite rejection of God, the Holy Ghost, and prophetic teachings. Another letter recounts military defeat, deaths, and grave cruelty by both the Lamanites and their own people, urging Moroni to remain faithful as destruction threatens. Finally, Moroni seals the record, calls the Lamanites and all people to remember God’s mercy, seek truth through sincere prayer and the Holy Ghost, cultivate faith, hope, and charity, come unto Christ, receive grace, deny ungodliness, and become holy through Christ’s blood.

l: Moroni, The Book of Moroni
s: Moroni is a Nephite man, prophet, and son of Mormon who remains alive after abridging the account of the people of Jared. Refusing to deny Christ, he conceals himself from the Lamanites and wanders to preserve his life while writing for their future benefit. Called by the Lord Jesus Christ to the ministry, he receives Mormon’s letters, is urged to correct the baptism of little children, labor diligently, stay faithful, and possibly receive sacred records. He writes to the Lamanites, exhorts them to remember the Lord’s mercy, and seals the records. Expecting resurrection, he anticipates resting in paradise until spirit and body reunite, then meeting the Lamanites before the bar of God.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Moroni
s: The Lamanites are a people involved in fierce internal wars, stirred by hatred and Satan, who kill Nephites unwilling to deny Christ. In conflict with the writer’s people, they take women and children prisoner, kill their husbands and fathers, feed the prisoners their relatives’ flesh, and give them little water. They are described as without civilization, yet less wicked than the writer’s people, whose atrocities exceed theirs. Moroni writes to the Lamanites and exhorts them to remember the Lord, ask God sincerely with faith in Christ, come to Christ, seek good gifts, deny ungodliness, and be perfected and sanctified through God’s grace and Christ’s blood.

l: wars, The Book of Moroni
s: are exceedingly fierce [among the Lamanites themselves] The wars are exceedingly fierce among the Lamanites and occur among themselves.

l: Nephites, The Book of Moroni
s: Nephites reject great knowledge, deny the Holy Ghost, and oppose God-given authority; pride threatens destruction unless they repent, while Lamanites kill those refusing to deny Christ.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: Jesus Christ is Christ, the Son of God, the Eternal Father, Redeemer, Lord, God, and the unchanging author and finisher of faith. He dwells eternally in heaven, yet his sufferings, death, shed blood, mercy, and long-suffering make salvation, remission of sins, and hope of glory possible. All good things and good gifts come through him; he gives power to those who have faith in him, claims and advocates for them, and calls all people to repentance, baptism, and perfection in him. The records begin with Moroni’s refusal to deny Christ amid killing of Nephites who likewise refuse. Christ then speaks to his twelve chosen disciples, directing them to call on the Father in his name and give the Holy Ghost by laying on hands. Priests and teachers preach repentance and remission of sins through him, while prayers address the Father in the name of the Son, call for obedience to his commandments, and remember his blood shed for those who drink wine. Baptized people take Christ’s name, serve him to the end, and rely on his merits alone. Mormon identifies him as Redeemer, Lord, and God, teaching that little children are whole through Christ and freed from Adam’s curse. The writer trusts Christ to save and lift his son. Finally, Christ is known by the Holy Ghost, gives spiritual gifts, and invites people to come unto and be perfected in him.

l: Lord, The Book of Moroni
s: The Lord Jesus Christ sits at the right hand of God’s power until all things become subject to him. From Adam’s creation onward, the Lord has been merciful to the children of men; the writer prays that his grace will abide forever.

l: disciples (Christ's disciples), The Book of Moroni
s: The disciples, apostles who heard Christ's words at his first appearing, call on the Father in mighty prayer, gain power, and give the Holy Ghost by laying on hands.

l: God, the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni
s: God, the Eternal Father, is called on in the name of Christ through mighty prayer, is addressed before priest and teacher ordinations, and fulfills covenants with the house of Israel.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Moroni
s: The Holy Ghost is a power and Comforter that works in the hearts of people. Disciples give it in Christ’s name by laying on hands, and it falls upon those people; it also gives the disciples power to ordain priests and teachers. It is promised to remain with those who take Jesus Christ’s name, remember him, and keep his commandments, including those who drink the wine. It cleanses those received unto baptism and leads church meetings, enabling preaching, exhorting, prayer, supplication, and singing. It can have place in hearts and helps the meek and lowly confess that Jesus is the Christ. It brings the word of the Lord to Mormon, visits repentant people with hope and perfect love, and manifests truth to sincere people with faith in Christ, enabling knowledge of truth and that Christ is.

l: multitude, The Book of Moroni
s: did_not_hear Christ's words [at Christ's first appearing] The multitude does not hear Christ's words when he speaks them to the disciples.

l: prayer, The Book of Moroni
s: is_practiced meetings [oft] The church meets often to fast and pray, and its members are kept continually watchful unto prayer while relying upon the merits of Christ.

l: disciples (elders of the church), The Book of Moroni
s: Disciples, called elders of the church, possess power of the Holy Ghost and pray to the Father in Jesus Christ’s name before laying hands to ordain priests and teachers according to God’s gifts and callings.

l: church of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: The church of Christ receives the administration of the flesh and blood of Christ, kneeling with elders or priests in prayer and partaking often of bread and wine in remembrance of the Lord Jesus. It numbers baptized people cleansed by the Holy Ghost, records and nourishes them by the good word of God, and meets often to fast, pray, and care for souls. It requires no iniquity among members, removes the unrepentant, and forgives those who sincerely repent. It consists of peaceable followers of Christ with hope to enter the Lord’s rest.

l: priests, The Book of Moroni
s: Priests are ordained ministers who preach repentance and remission of sins through Jesus Christ by enduring faith in his name, and administer Christ’s flesh and blood to the church according to his commandments.

l: teachers, The Book of Moroni
s: Teachers were ordained ministers who preached repentance and remission of sins through Jesus Christ, calling for worthy baptism and enduring faith to the end.

l: God, The Book of Moroni
s: God is the Father who knows all things and is the source of every good thing. He permits Mormon to speak, gives the Spirit of Christ to every person to distinguish good from evil, and sends angels and prophets to reveal Christ’s coming. Prayer is directed to God the Father in the name of Jesus, with real intent of heart. He is not partial or changeable; his mercy saves little children and those without the law. God is asked to judge the people and hide their sins from his face, while the writer fears being smitten. In the end, God manifests truth through the Holy Ghost, gives gifts, works according to faith, and confirms Moroni’s writings.

l: children of men, The Book of Moroni
s: The children of men can know good and evil through Christ’s Spirit, receive good things, mercy, angels, faith, the Holy Ghost, salvation, and become sons of God. Gifts come according to faith, while unbelief and iniquity can remove God’s gifts and power and bring despair.

l: ordination, The Book of Moroni
s: Ordination is performed through prayer to the Father in Jesus Christ’s name, laying on of hands, and appropriate words; priests and teachers receive it according to God’s gifts and callings by the Holy Ghost.

l: repentance, The Book of Moroni
s: Repentance is required for sin and for return unto God, especially for those under condemnation. It is witnessed before baptism; its first fruit is baptism following faith. Through commandments it brings remission of sins, then meekness, the Holy Ghost, hope, and perfect love. Those committing iniquity must repent and confess to be forgiven; without repentance, people perish.

l: remission of sins, The Book of Moroni
s: Remission of sins comes through the shedding of the blood of Christ in the covenant of the Father, allowing people to become holy and without spot.

l: faith, The Book of Moroni
s: Faith in Christ is required for hope and salvation in the kingdom of God. Through Christ, it enables people to lay hold of good, receive answers to prayer, perform miracles, receive angelic ministry, know truth through the Holy Ghost, and do things expedient to Christ. It leads to baptism unto fulfilling the commandments and is shown through meekness.

l: elders, The Book of Moroni
s: Elders baptize those worthy through repentance and administer Christ’s flesh and blood to the church according to commandments.

l: flesh and blood of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: The flesh and blood of Christ are administered to the church according to Christ’s commandments.

l: commandments of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: are_given_by Jesus Christ [to those who partake of the bread] The commandments of Christ govern the administration of the flesh and blood of Christ. Participants witness that they are willing to keep these commandments.

l: bread, The Book of Moroni
s: is_used_for remembrance of the Lord Jesus [in meetings] Bread is prayed over so that it may be blessed and sanctified to the souls of all who partake of it. Those who eat it are to remember the body of Jesus Christ.

l: body of Jesus Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: is_remembered_through bread [by those who partake of it] The body of Jesus Christ is to be remembered by those who partake of the bread.

l: administering the flesh and blood of Christ, The Book of Moroni
s: A manner of elders and priests: administering Christ’s flesh and blood according to Christ’s commandments.
